title: Virtual Worlds with Real Physics and Robot Video Generation

opening.say: Good morning, and welcome to Mono Radio. It's Monday, November ninth, and here's your morning briefing.
opening.show: Good morning, and welcome to Mono Radio. It's Monday, November 9.

opening.say: Today we have five stories from the worlds of A I and three D.
opening.show: Today we have five stories from the worlds of AI and 3D.

news.label: Four New Cosmos 3 Models
points: Four models built on Cosmos 3 Nano
Predicting video from robot arm motion
details: Four open-weight models built on Cosmos 3 Nano have been released.
They include Sim-Bimanual, which predicts the next video frames from the motions of a two-armed robot.
There are also models that generate multi-camera and LiDAR data, and post-training recipes are available too.

lines.say: Let's start with NVIDIA, which has released four new open models built on Cosmos three.
lines.show: Let's start with NVIDIA and its new Cosmos 3 models.

lines.say: What's fun is that they can predict video from a two-armed robot's movements, and even generate data for self-driving.
lines.show: They can generate video that follows a robot's movements.

link.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
link.description: A Blog post by NVIDIA on Hugging Face

news.label: Anthropic on Memory Cleanup
points: Logs, notes, and knowledge kept apart
details: It's a method where an agent looks back over its past run logs and consolidates key insights into memory.
Conversation logs, notes, structured knowledge, and the context loaded next time are handled separately.
It shows that saving selected current goals and verified rules works better than recording everything.

lines.say: Next up is Anthropic, with an explainer on a method called dreaming, where agents tidy up their own memory.
lines.show: Next, Anthropic and a method called dreaming for agent memory.

lines.say: The takeaway is that keeping your current goals and verified rules works better than saving everything.
lines.show: Choosing what to keep beats saving everything.

link.title: The components of agent memory
link.description: For Claude to learn from experience, it has to decide what’s worth remembering before it knows what’s next. Here’s how “dreaming” helps it organize memory and correct mistakes.

news.label: Speeding Up FLUX 3 Inference
details: A guide has been published on speeding up image generation and image editing with TensorRT LLM VisualGen.
In tests at 2048 by 2048 on a single B200, text to image is up to 3.46 times faster, and image to image is up to 4.45 times faster.
It also includes an example of serving through an OpenAI-compatible image generation endpoint.

lines.say: Here's another one from NVIDIA, a new way to make the image model FLUX three run faster.
lines.show: Another from NVIDIA: a way to make FLUX 3 run faster.

lines.say: Depending on the setup, it's up to more than four times faster, which is a big jump.
lines.show: Depending on the setup, it's over four times faster.

link.title: Speed Up Image Generation with FLUX 3 Image Klein on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs | NVIDIA Technical Blog
link.description: When deploying diffusion models in design tools, image editors, and visual production workflows, developers must account for inference latency. Generating an image requires multiple sequential passes…

news.label: Snapmaker U1 Launches in Japan
points: On sale in Japan from November 6
Prints up to 270 mm per side
details: The official distributor in Japan announced it, and it sells for 154,000 yen including tax.
Instead of sharing one nozzle and purging, it uses SnapSwap, which swaps the whole head in about five seconds.
It supports prints up to 270 by 270 by 270 millimeters. The waste reduction of up to 85 percent is based on the maker's own comparison tests.

lines.say: On to three D printing. The Snapmaker U one has gone on sale in Japan.
lines.show: On to 3D printing: the Snapmaker U1 is on sale in Japan.

lines.say: It swaps the whole head in about five seconds, so there's less waste when changing colors.
lines.show: It swaps heads in about 5 seconds, so color changes waste less.

news.label: SimReady Central Is Live
details: More than 2,000 OpenUSD assets, including robot arms, grippers, and warehouse equipment, are available on Hugging Face.
They carry simulation properties such as collision shapes, mass, friction, and joint limits.
Searching in natural language and assembling scenes with A I agents are also envisioned.

lines.say: Last up is NVIDIA again, with SimReady Central, which offers over two thousand free three D assets with physics information.
lines.show: Last, NVIDIA again: free 3D assets with physics information.

lines.say: They include collision shapes and mass, so they look ready to drop straight into a simulation.
lines.show: With mass included, they look easy to use in simulation.
